model: Performance Center M&P M2.0 Competitor HD
sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 (Copyright © 2022 Smith & Wesson Inc. All rights reserved.)
cleanIntro: Smith & Wesson's manual for the M&P9 M2.0 Metal Frame and Performance Center Competitor pistols is the book Smith & Wesson pairs with the Competitor HD. The takedown needs no trigger pull: the frame tool drops the sear deactivation lever and the takedown lever rotates. Where the Competitor differs from the standard metal frame, the book says so, and so does this guide. Every step below carries the manual's words and the page they are on.

steps.title: Make sure this is the book for your pistol
steps.action: This procedure comes from Smith & Wesson's manual for the M&P9 M2.0 Metal Frame and Performance Center Competitor pistols. The book does not print the words "Competitor HD"; Smith & Wesson's own product listing for the Competitor HD names this manual as its owner's manual. Where the book gives the Competitor its own instruction, follow that one and not the standard-model one beside it.
steps.prose: The book is written for two pistols at once and branches between them on the same page: the standard metal frame and the PC Competitor have different frame tools, and only the Competitor has a magwell flare and an extended magazine catch. Read the label on each figure before you copy what it shows. The polymer-frame M&P pistols are not covered by this book; they have their own manuals.
steps.quote: adds a magwell flare and a slightly different frame tool.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Field Stripping / Disassembly Continued, p.28

steps.title: Magazine out, slide back, chamber cleared
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard. Depress the magazine catch and remove the magazine, then grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear and briskly draw it fully rearward to extract any cartridge from the chamber and throw it clear.
steps.prose: Magazine first, always: racking the slide with a loaded magazine still seated simply chambers the next round. Brisk matters too, because a slide eased back can let an extracted round drop back onto the feed ramp. Keep your hand clear of the ejection port; the book says covering it can interfere with ejection.
steps.quote: briskly draw the slide fully rearward in order to extract any cartridge from the barrel chamber and clear it from the pistol.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Unloading, p.25

steps.title: Lock the slide open and look twice
steps.action: Let the slide move slightly forward from its rearmost position while pressing upward on the slide stop, so the slide locks open. Look into the barrel chamber, then look down through the magazine well, and satisfy yourself no ammunition remains in the pistol.
steps.prose: Two windows, two separate facts: the chamber tells you the barrel is empty, the magazine well tells you nothing is left to feed it. The slide has to stay locked open for the takedown that follows, so this is also the position you strip from. Empty the magazine as well, pressing each cartridge forward and out with the bullet end pointed away from you.
steps.quote: Look down through the magazine well. Verify that no ammunition remains in the pistol
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Unloading, p.25

steps.title: Frame tool out of the grip
steps.action: With the slide locked open and the pistol confirmed empty, take the frame tool out of the bottom of the grip by turning it 90 degrees and pulling it out of the frame. On the Competitor the tool is the Competitor's own: turn it to unlock it, then withdraw it. The book notes a 5/32-inch hex wrench can be used to lock and unlock it.
steps.prose: The Competitor's frame tool is not the standard one, and the book draws the two side by side so you can tell them apart. If it will not turn by hand, use the hex wrench the book names rather than a screwdriver blade, which will chew the head. The tool is the part you use for the next step, so keep it to hand.
steps.quote: Remove the frame tool from the bottom of the grip by turning it 90 degrees and pulling it out of the frame
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.26

steps.title: Palmswell insert off, bottom first
steps.action: Tip the interchangeable palmswell backstrap insert away from the frame, starting at the bottom, until the tab at the top lets go of the frame.
steps.prose: Bottom first is the whole trick. The tab at the top hooks into the frame, and prising the insert from the top loads that tab in the direction it is built to resist. The book also cautions that some solvents can damage the insert material, so it stays off the bench while you clean.
steps.quote: Remove the interchangeable palmswell back strap insert from the frame by tipping it away from the frame - bottom first to release the tab at the top that engages the frame
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Field Stripping / Disassembly Continued, p.27

steps.title: Push the sear deactivation lever down
steps.action: Using the frame tool, or a similar device, push the sear deactivation lever down into the lowered position. Look for it through the ejection port with the slide locked open; it is coloured yellow or green.
steps.prose: This lever is why the takedown never asks you to pull the trigger: lowered, it takes the sear out of the way so the slide can come off. If it will not go down, do not force it and do not fall back on pressing the trigger. Check first that the slide is still locked open, because the lever is reached through the open ejection port.
steps.caution: The sear deactivation lever is yellow/green in color.
steps.quote: to push the sear deactivation lever down into the lowered position
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Field Stripping / Disassembly Continued, p.27

steps.title: Rotate the takedown lever clockwise
steps.action: Rotate the takedown lever clockwise until it stops.
steps.prose: The lever turns with the slide still locked back. If it feels solid, the slide has most likely crept forward off the slide stop; lock it open again rather than forcing the lever.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Field Stripping / Disassembly Continued, p.27

steps.title: Slide off the frame, controlling the recoil spring
steps.action: Grasp the slide from the top, pull it slightly rearward to disengage the slide stop, then run it forward off the frame, keeping control of the recoil spring and guide rod assembly as it comes.
steps.prose: The recoil spring assembly is under compression as the slide leaves the rails. Hold the slide from the top as the book shows, so your hand is over the spring and not behind it, and keep the muzzle end away from your face.
steps.quote: remove the slide from the frame by pulling it slightly rearward (to disengage the slide stop) then forward while being careful to control the recoil spring and guide rod assembly
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Field Stripping / Disassembly Continued, p.27

steps.title: Recoil spring out, then the barrel
steps.action: Lift the recoil spring assembly out from below the barrel, then remove the barrel from the bottom of the slide.
steps.prose: Note which end of the spring assembly went where: the smaller end sits at the muzzle and the larger end bears against the barrel lug, and it goes back the same way. With the spring out, the barrel comes out of the bottom of the slide with nothing holding it.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring from below the barrel
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Field Stripping / Disassembly Continued, p.28

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly, frame, palmswell insert, frame tool and magazine. On the Competitor the magwell flare is still on the grip; the book gives its own removal, in Deep Clean.
steps.prose: The book draws its line here in capitals: the striker, the sear and the other fire control parts stay in the pistol. Past this point, the book sends you to a qualified gunsmith using genuine Smith & Wesson parts. These parts reach everything the cleaning section asks for.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR HANDGUN BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING PROCESS OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Field Stripping / Disassembly Continued, p.28

deepSteps.title: The Competitor's magwell flare comes off
deepSteps.action: On the PC Competitor the magwell flare can be removed for cleaning or replacement. Before you start, remove the magazine and confirm the pistol is unloaded and the chamber is empty.
deepSteps.prose: The flare is the Competitor's own part; the standard metal frame does not have one, so this section of the book applies only to it. The flare collects grit and fouling where the magazine enters, which is why the book gives the owner its removal.
deepSteps.quote: The magwell flare can be removed for cleaning or replacement.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — PC™ Competitor™ Magwell Flare, p.33
deepSteps.warn: ALWAYS ENSURE THAT YOUR FIREARM IS UNLOADED BEFORE BEGINNING ANY CLEANING OR MAINTENANCE.

deepSteps.title: Turn the retainer and withdraw it
deepSteps.action: Turn the retainer and withdraw it from the frame.
deepSteps.prose: The book points this step at the same figure it uses for the Competitor's frame tool, so the part you turn here is the one at the base of the grip. If it is already out from the field strip, go straight to sliding the flare off.
deepSteps.quote: Turn the retainer (FIGURE 66) and withdraw it from the frame.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — PC™ Competitor™ Magwell Flare, p.33

deepSteps.title: Slide the flare forward off the grip
deepSteps.action: Slide the magwell flare forward, off the grip frame.
deepSteps.prose: Forward is the direction the book gives. A groove in the flare engages the frame edge from the front of the pistol, so the flare slides rather than pries; if it binds, check the retainer is fully out instead of levering it.
deepSteps.quote: Slide the magwell flare forward off the grip frame
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — PC™ Competitor™ Magwell Flare, p.33

deepSteps.title: Refit the flare, aligned to the grip
deepSteps.action: Reinstall the flare by reversing the removal. Align it with the base of the grip frame, then reinstall the retainer and pivot the lever to lock it.
deepSteps.prose: Alignment is the thing to check: a flare that sits crooked on the grip will catch the magazine on the way in. Lock the retainer before you rely on it, then seat and drop an empty magazine to confirm nothing drags.
deepSteps.quote: Reinstall the retainer and pivot the lever to lock it in place.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — PC™ Competitor™ Magwell Flare, p.33

deepSteps.title: Magazine: depress the floor plate catch
deepSteps.action: With the magazine empty, use a small tool to depress the floor plate catch through the hole in the floor plate. The book shows several floor plate shapes; the hole is there on each.
deepSteps.prose: The spring inside is pushing the catch and the floor plate down the whole time, so keep a thumb over the bottom of the tube from here on. Safety glasses, as the book asks for magazine work.
deepSteps.quote: Using a small tool, depress floor plate catch through the hole in the floor plate
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Magazines — Magazine Disassembly, p.36
deepSteps.warn: THE MAGAZINE SPRING IS UNDER PRESSURE. CONTROL THE SPRING AND FOLLOWER SO THAT THEY DO NOT FLY OUT AND CAUSE INJURY.

deepSteps.title: Slide the floor plate off, holding the catch in
deepSteps.action: Slide the floor plate forward off the tube while holding the floor plate catch in the tube against spring pressure. Then take out the floor plate catch, the spring and the follower through the bottom of the tube.
deepSteps.prose: Your thumb on the catch is what keeps the spring in the tube while the floor plate leaves. Ease the pressure off slowly once the plate is clear, and note the orientation of each part as it comes out, because the book asks for exactly that orientation on reassembly.
deepSteps.quote: Slide floor plate forward off of the tube while holding floor plate catch in the tube against spring pressure
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Magazines — Magazine Disassembly, p.36

deepSteps.title: Reassemble the magazine the way it came apart
deepSteps.action: Put the magazine spring, follower and floor plate catch back into the tube in exactly the orientation they came out in. Holding the floor plate catch in the tube, slide the floor plate onto the tube's base until the catch engages it.
deepSteps.prose: A spring turned around or a follower in backwards gives a magazine that looks fine and feeds badly. That is why the book insists on the original orientation rather than any orientation that fits.
deepSteps.quote: in exactly the same orientation as they were in when they were first removed during disassembly.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Magazines — Magazine Assembly, p.37

deepSteps.title: Prove the floor plate is locked
deepSteps.action: Push on the floor plate as if trying to slide it off the tube. It must not move.
deepSteps.prose: A floor plate that is not caught can let go under spring pressure, and the magazine empties its spring and follower onto the ground. This push test is the check the book gives; do it every time the magazine has been apart.
deepSteps.quote: Verify that the floor plate is locked in place by exerting some pressure on the floor plate
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual for M&P®9 M2.0™ Metal Frame and Performance Center™ COMPETITOR™ Pistols — REV: M&P9_M2_METAL_FRAME_063022 — Magazines — Magazine Assembly, p.37

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Remove excess firing residue from the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish by running a dry cotton patch through the bore to remove the residue and solvent
Use a cleaning rod long enough to push the brush and jag completely through the barrel

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME AND MAGWELL
tasks: Clean the exterior of the pistol with a non-abrasive cleaning cloth
On the Competitor, clean the magwell flare and the base of the grip frame it seats on
Remove every trace of cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints from the outside surfaces; finger moisture left behind can start corrosion
Keep solvent off the palmswell insert: the book cautions that some solvents may damage the insert material

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION — EIGHT POINTS, ONE DROP EACH
tasks: Smith & Wesson names eight lubrication points and asks for a single drop of high-quality firearm lubricant at each
Do not over-lubricate: excess lubricant collects unburned powder and carbon residue that can interfere with functioning
After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts, inside and out, with a high-quality gun oil
In cold climates, use an oil of a weight that will not congeal

cleaning.name: AVOID, AND BEFORE STORAGE
tasks: ⚠ Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on the pistol
Do not store the pistol in leather or heavy cloth, or with a plug in the barrel
For long storage, oil the bore, chamber and internal mechanism and coat the external metal with an anti-rust oil; clean it again before use
Check for signs of wear every time you clean it; if wear is noted, do not use the pistol and have it checked by Smith & Wesson or a qualified gunsmith

reassembly: Replace the barrel in the slide so the muzzle is flush with the end of the slide and the barrel lug is turned up, away from the ejection port.

Fit the recoil spring assembly with its smaller end in the slide's guide housing at the muzzle and its larger end compressed slightly against the barrel lug, and check it is centred and seated, not sitting misaligned.

Holding the slide and recoil spring guide firmly, with the takedown lever down, put the rear of the slide onto the front frame rails and pull it back onto the rear rails until it is fully rearward. Press up on the slide stop and let the slide come slightly forward to lock it open.

Rotate the takedown lever fully upward before letting the slide move forward. Refit the palmswell insert, then replace the Competitor's frame tool in the base of the grip and turn it to lock (a 5/32-inch hex wrench can be used).
Pull the slide to the rear and release it so it carries fully forward, then insert the empty magazine: that returns the sear deactivation lever to normal operation.
fncheck: With the pistol unloaded and the chamber visually confirmed empty: draw the slide fully rearward with an empty magazine seated, and check the slide stop moves up and holds the slide open, as the book's assembly check asks. Check the takedown lever is fully up. Confirm the frame tool is turned and locked in the grip and, on the Competitor, that the magwell flare is aligned and its retainer locked. Seat an empty magazine, pull on it to confirm the magazine catch holds, then press the catch and check the magazine drops free.
